project.name: Example Shop
project.eyebrow: Architecture reference · example data, replace it
intro: Example Shop sells products online. A customer places an order; the shop charges the card and records the order.
Click any box in the map to open its details. A controller shows the steps of each operation; every underlined type is a model you can open.

facts.html: Orders are created only after the payment succeeds.
Payments go through an external gateway behind a provider interface.

layers.title: Controller
layers.what: One method per thing a user or system does. It sequences services and owns the transaction.

layers.title: Service
layers.what: One capability: its rules and the I/O it owns.

entries.name: HTTP API
entries.what: JSON endpoints for the web shop. Each route parses its input and calls one controller operation.

controllers.name: CheckoutController
controllers.what: Turns a cart into a paid order.
why: A customer expects one action that both charges the card and records the order. Neither the payment service nor the order service can own that sequence alone, because a service never calls another service.
This controller is the only place where payment and ordering meet. The HTTP API calls it; the order service never learns how payment works.

ops.name: checkout
ops.what: Charges the cart total once, then records the paid order in one transaction; a declined card creates no order.

payments.what: Charges cards through the payment gateway and returns a receipt.

Charger.name: charge
Charger.what: Charges the amount once; a declined card is a failure value, not a receipt.

OrderWriter.name: create
OrderWriter.what: Records a paid order for the cart's lines.

repos.name: PaymentGateway
repos.note: SDK client of the payment provider.

stores.name: Payment provider
stores.what: Charges cards. Reached only through the PaymentGateway provider.

models.title: Cart
models.what: The lines a customer wants to buy and their total.
models.def: type Cart = { lines: { sku: string; quantity: number }[]; total: Money };

models.title: Order
models.def: type Order = { id: string; cart: Cart; receipt: Receipt };

models.title: Money · Receipt
models.what: An amount in a currency, and the proof that it was charged.
models.def:
type Money = { cents: number; currency: string };
type Receipt = { id: string; amount: Money };
